context.title: Q-polynomial quotient conjecture for taut distance-regular graphs
context.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a taut distance-regular graph with odd diameter $D\geq 5$. By the source's stated theorem, $\Gamma$ is an antipodal $2$-cover; hence its antipodal quotient is defined. **Q-polynomial quotient conjecture.** The antipodal quotient of $\Gamma$ is $Q$-polynomial. This proposes a structural property for the antipodal quotients of taut distance-regular graphs of odd diameter at least $5$; the source gives no resolution.
context.source_name: Mark S. MacLean and Paul Terwilliger, “Taut distance-regular graphs and the subconstituent algebra”, arXiv:math/0508399 (2005).
context.references:

context.title: Conjecture that complete graphs are strongly GT
context.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, possibly with loops in $H$. Write $\hom(G,H)$ for the number of graph homomorphisms from $G$ to $H$. A graph $H$ is **strongly GT** if, for every graph $G$,

$$
\hom(G\sqcup G,H)\leq \hom(G\times K_2,H).
$$

**Strongly GT conjecture for complete graphs.** For $q\geq 3$, the complete graph $K_q$ is strongly GT.

For $H=K_q$, this would imply the desired upper bound on the number of proper $q$-colorings of an $N$-vertex, $d$-regular graph. The source explains that $K_q$ is not a bipartite swapping target because it contains an induced triangle, but conjectures that it is nevertheless strongly GT. The resolution status is not specified.
context.source_name: Yufei Zhao, “The Bipartite Swapping Trick on Graph Homomorphisms”, arXiv:1104.3704 (2011).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3704

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2011).

context.title: Volume-partition enumeration conjecture for a permutation pattern
context.literal_statement:
Regard two permutations as equivalent if they give the same **volume partition**. Let

$$
\mathbf{p}=\substack{\displaystyle{\nivl{\scriptstyle 1{\kern 1.75pt}2}{\kern 1.75pt}\vinb{\scriptstyle 3}} \\ \displaystyle{\vinb{\scriptstyle 1{\kern 1.75pt}2{\kern 1.75pt}3}}}.
$$

Let $\widetilde{{\mathfrak A}}_n(\mathbf{p})$ denote the corresponding set of equivalence-class representatives. **Volume-partition enumeration conjecture.** The cardinalities satisfy

$$
\left|\widetilde{{\mathfrak A}}_n(\mathbf{p})\right|=1,2,5,18,84,480,3240,25200,\ldots,
\qquad n=1,2,3,\ldots.
$$

From $n=2$ onward, these values are identified with A038720, the next-to-last diagonal of A038719, which counts chains in a specific poset. The conjecture concerns enumeration under volume-partition equivalence.

context.title: Defective list edge-colouring conjecture
context.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $d$ be an integer. Write $ch'_d(G)$ for the $d$-defective list chromatic index and $\chi'_d(G)$ for the $d$-defective edge chromatic number.

**Defective list edge-colouring conjecture.** For every graph $G$ and every integer $d$,

$$
ch'_d(G)=\chi'_d(G).
$$

This is a stronger defective analogue of the list edge-colouring conjecture; the source says it is proved for bipartite graphs, while the general assertion remains open.

context.title: Defective Goldberg-Seymour conjecture
context.literal_statement:
Let $d\in\mathbb N^*$ and let $G$ be a graph. Define

$$
\Gamma_d(G)=\max\left\{\left\lceil \frac{|E(G[X])|}{\left\lfloor d|X|/2\right\rfloor}\right\rceil\mathrel{:}X\subseteq V(G)\right\}.
$$

**Defective Goldberg-Seymour conjecture.** Every graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\chi'_d(G)\leq \max\left\{\Gamma_d(G),\left\lceil \frac{\Delta(G)+1}{d}\right\rceil\right\}.
$$

This is proposed as a generalization of the Goldberg-Seymour bound to defective edge colouring; no proof or counterexample is supplied in the source.

context.title: Adjacency conjecture for partition m-hemimetrics
context.literal:
Let $V_n$ be the ground set, and let $\alpha(S_1,\dots,S_{m+1})$ and $\alpha(T_1,\dots,T_{m+1})$ be two partition $m$-hemimetrics on $V_n$. Two rays are adjacent when they generate a two-dimensional face of the cone, that is, when they are adjacent in the skeleton of $P_n^m$. **Adjacency conjecture for partition m-hemimetrics.** The two partition $m$-hemimetrics $\alpha(S_1,\dots,S_{m+1})$ and $\alpha(T_1,\dots,T_{m+1})$ are nonadjacent in the skeleton of $P_n^m$ if and only if there exist six different subsets $S_i,S_j,S_k$ and $T_{i'},T_{j'},T_{k'}$ such that

$$
S_i\mathbin{\cup}S_j=T_{k'}
$$

and

$$
S_k=T_{i'}\mathbin{\cup}T_{j'}.
$$

The conjecture holds for $m=1$, when all cut semimetrics are adjacent; for $n-m=2$, when the graph is $J(m+2,2)$; and for $(m,n)=(2,5)$ and $(3,6)$.
